% Pattern: attach/head. A proof whose head is a braced group after
% \begin{proof}, as {Proof of Lemma~\ref{a}.}, in place of the option,
% proves what the head names. Seen in the gold pilot (set X).
% want lemma-1 statement/lemma 1.1
% want theorem-1 statement/theorem 1.2
% want proof-1 proof - proves=lemma-1
% want proof-2 proof - proves=theorem-1
\documentclass{article}
\usepackage{amsthm}
\newtheorem{theorem}{Theorem}[section]
\newtheorem{lemma}[theorem]{Lemma}
\begin{document}
\section{One}

\begin{lemma}\label{l:sup}
A bounded set of reals has a least upper bound.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}\label{t:main}
Every bounded monotone sequence converges.
\end{theorem}

\section{Proofs}

\begin{proof}{Proof of Lemma~\ref{l:sup}.}
This is the completeness axiom.
\end{proof}

\vspace{1cm}
\begin{proof}{\bf Proof of Theorem~\ref{t:main}.}
Take the least upper bound of the terms.
\end{proof}
\end{document}
